# $T_n\equiv\star3$ and $S_n\equiv\star3$ against nim heaps, for every even $n\ge12$ resp. odd $n\ge13$ (whole-board game on $C_n$)

**Summary**
1. Theorem (nim-heap outcome equivalence): in the whole-board game on $C_n$ (race rule "count", e.p. on, an e.p.-capturable pawn is not passed, game ends at the first passed pawn), the $(n+1)$-pawn rings $T_n = (B4\,W2)^{(n-10)/2}\,B5\,W2\,W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2$ (even $n\ge12$) and $S_n = B4\,B6\,W3\,(W2\,B4)^{(n-11)/2}\,W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2$ (odd $n\ge13$) satisfy: for every heap $h<256$, $G+\star h$ has the outcome of $\star3+\star h$ (P for $h=3$, N otherwise). This is written $G\equiv\star3$. It is not a claim of equality of partizan games in standard CGT (section 3, H7).
2. The proof is the insertion proof of Section S13 (Lemmas 1-3 there, with the written-out Lemma 3 of Note 1 of Section S15, its section 2b), at one fixed cut per family: $T$: $c=4$, $n_0=20$; $S$: $c=7$, $n_0=23$. The $T$ wall is B4/W2 on files $0..n-11$; the $S$ wall is W2/B4 on files $3..n-9$, after the leading $B4\,B6\,W3$. Both are W2/B4 walls in the sense of type E of Section S13; no colour reversal is used.
3. C1: the reduced game at the base has 1305 nodes ($T_{20}$) resp. 40445 nodes ($S_{23}$), no e.p. flag, no passed pawn, zone $\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-2\}$ resp. $\{0,1,2\}\cup\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-1\}$, signature NNNPNN ($h=0..5$); files $c-4..c+5$ are exact pattern files in every node; $\mathrm{ins}_c$ maps the graph isomorphically for $n\ge n_0$. C2: every size below $n_0$, i.e. $n=12,14,16,18$ ($T$) and $n=13,15,17,19,21$ ($S$), by direct search. E.p. convention: canonical (a flag only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square).
4. Status: PROVED for $n\ge n_0$ given Lemmas 1-3 of Section S13, 2b and the finite checks C1, C2; CHECKED-2 for the base cases.
5. $T_{12}$ and $S_{13}$ are the smallest (the $n=10$ ($T$) and $n=11$ ($S$) members are not $\equiv\star3$).

**How this note was checked.** The finite parts were computed by three independently written programs (section 0): A, the C program of Section S13, gave the reduced games, the pump and, through Lemma 1, the base-case signatures; E, a Python engine written from the rules, rebuilt the reduced graphs of C1, checked the hypotheses of Lemmas 2 and 3 on every node and ran direct searches for the smaller base cases; R, a Python program written from the rules by one of the referees (standard library only), rebuilt the reduced graphs, both insertion steps per family and every base case by direct search. The hand proof was checked by two independent AI referees, both from model vendors other than that of the model that wrote the note, one for the logic and one for the logic and the finite facts (with R); both found it sound after corrections that are incorporated in the text (most importantly, the theorem is stated as nim-heap outcome equivalence, H7). No human referee has checked it yet.

**Scope.** Proved: the whole-board game, race rule "count", canonical e.p. convention, and outcome equivalence to $\star3$ against nim-heap addends only (H7). Not claimed: equality to $\star3$ as a standard partizan game, the component-sum model, another race rule, or equivalence against arbitrary addends rather than nim-heaps. Race-rule sensitivity and the component-sum model were not examined for $T_n$, $S_n$. The sizes $n<n_0$ are covered by C2, not by the induction.

## 0. Claims and labels

PROVED = by hand, given the lemmas. CHECKED-2 = two or more independently written programs agree. COMPUTED-1 = one program. Programs: **A** = the program `rg.c` of Section S13 (via `pump_verify.py`); **E** = `verify_compute/myeng.py` (written from the rules); **R** = `research/star3_check/independent.py` (written from the rules by another AI model, standard library only, imports none of `cylcgt`, `rg`, `myeng.py`). A drives the pump; E drives `research/star3_proof/check_S3T3.py` and `base_S3T3.py`; R rebuilds the reduced graphs, both insertion steps and every base case.

## 1. Setting

Model, classes T/L/P/K, reduced game: as in Section S13 and in section 1 of Note 1 of Section S15 (race rule "count"). A **pattern file** is a wall file holding exactly its starting pawn and nothing else. E.p. convention: a flag is recorded only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square of the double step; a flag nobody could use is dropped. "No flag" in C1, H4, H6 means this canonical convention.

Files $0..n-1$, $n$ even $\ge12$ ($T$) or odd $\ge13$ ($S$):

- $T_n$: $(B4\,W2)^{(n-10)/2}$ on files $0..n-11$, then $B5$ ($n-10$), $W2$ ($n-9$), $W6B7$ ($n-8$), $W3$ ($n-7$), $B7$ ($n-6$), $B6$ ($n-5$), $W3$ ($n-4$), $W2$ ($n-3$), $B6$ ($n-2$), $W2$ ($n-1$). The tail occupies 10 files and holds 11 pawns ($W6B7$ is two pawns), so the ring has $(n-10)+11=n+1$ pawns. **Wall** = files $0..n-11$ (length $n-10$, even), $B4$ on even files, $W2$ on odd files, $B4$ at the left end and $W2$ at the right end (file $n-11$ is odd since $n$ is even).
- $S_n$: $B4$ ($0$), $B6$ ($1$), $W3$ ($2$), then $(W2\,B4)^{(n-11)/2}$ on files $3..n-9$, then $W6B7$ ($n-8$), $W3$ ($n-7$), $B7$ ($n-6$), $B6$ ($n-5$), $W3$ ($n-4$), $W2$ ($n-3$), $B6$ ($n-2$), $W2$ ($n-1$). The tail occupies 8 files and holds 9 pawns ($W6B7$ is two pawns), so the ring has $3+(n-11)+9=n+1$ pawns. **Wall** = files $3..n-9$ (length $n-11$, even), $W2$ on odd files, $B4$ on even files.

Zone $Z_n$ (the files that change in some node of the reduced game): $Z_n=\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-2\}$ ($T$), $Z_n=\{0,1,2\}\cup\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-1\}$ ($S$). For $T$ the zone lies outside the wall. For $S$ the zone contains the leading files $0,1,2$ and the last two wall files $n-10,n-9$; the **fixed run** of $S$ is the wall minus the zone, files $3..n-11$.

## 2. The cut and the base

By C1, in every node of the reduced game of $G_n$ ($n\ge n_0$) all files outside $Z_n$ keep their start content.

- $T$: the whole wall $0..n-11$ is pattern in every node. With $c=4$ the arc $A=\{c-4..c+5\}=\{0..9\}$ lies in the wall iff $n-11\ge9$, i.e. $n\ge20$; it does not fit at $n=18$. Set $n_0=20$. $\mathrm{ins}_4$ fixes files $0..4$ and shifts files $\ge5$ by 2, so $\mathrm{ins}_4(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$, and $c=4$ is admissible for every even $n\ge20$. Pump: insertion isomorphism $20\to22$ at $c=4$.
- $S$: not every wall file is pattern (the wall-end files $n-10,n-9$ are in the zone); the invariant used is that the fixed arc is pattern. With $c=7$ the arc $A=\{3..12\}$ lies in the fixed run $3..n-11$ iff $n-11\ge12$, i.e. $n\ge23$; at $n=21$ the zone files $11,12$ overlap the arc. Set $n_0=23$. $\mathrm{ins}_7$ fixes files $0..7$ and shifts files $\ge8$ by 2, so $\mathrm{ins}_7(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$ (at $S_{25}$: $\{0,1,2,15,16,18..24\}$), and the fixed run grows to $3..n-9$ of $S_{n+2}$; the arc stays disjoint from the zone for every odd $n\ge23$. Insertion isomorphisms $23\to25$ and $25\to27$ at $c=7$ are checked by E and R; A's pump line for $n=25$ is its check of $23\to25$ against the previous size, at $c=7$.

The ranges are sufficient, not necessary: E's control cuts give exact insertion for $c=5..8$ ($T$, $n=20$) and $c=8..11$ ($S$, $n=23$), first failure at $c=9$ ($T$) and $c=12$ ($S$).

## 3. Hypotheses of Lemmas 2 and 3

**H1 (wall, phase, ends).** $T$: the wall alternates $B4$ (even) / $W2$ (odd), a W2/B4 wall as in type E of Section S13; $\mathrm{ins}_4$ inserts after file 4 copies of files 5 ($W2$) and 4 ($B4$), so the new files 5, 6 continue the phase; $\mathrm{ins}_4(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ for $n\ge20$. $S$: the wall alternates $W2$ (odd) / $B4$ (even); $\mathrm{ins}_7$ inserts $B4$, $W2$ on the new files 8, 9, continuing the phase; $\mathrm{ins}_7(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ for $n\ge23$. The leading files $0,1,2$ of $S$ are in the zone, outside the arc, and fixed by $\mathrm{ins}_7$. Both walls match the case analysis of Lemma 2(b) in Section S13 directly (Lemma 2 only needs pattern files $j-1,j,j+1$ of alternating colour two ranks apart, in either phase), so no colour reversal is needed.

**H2 (no capture by $q$).** On a pattern triple, the capture squares of a $W2$ are on rank 3 while the adjacent $B4$ stand on rank 4, and the capture squares of a $B4$ are on rank 3 while the adjacent $W2$ stand on rank 2; so a wall pawn only pushes, and a $B4$ cannot take e.p. a $W2$ that has not moved (Note 1 of Section S15, H3). After a push an enemy pawn on an adjacent file is still ahead of it; a $W2$ double step to rank 4 beside a $B4$ leaves a live e.p. right and is not passed.

**H3 (windows at the two ends of the arc).** The central pawns are on files $c-3..c+4$; for $j\le c+2$ the window $j-1..j+3$, and for $j\ge c-1$ the window $j-3..j+1$, lies in the arc, which consists of pattern files in every node ($I_n$, H6). Lemma 2 is local to the window, so Lemma 2(b) makes every central move L or P for every $n\ge n_0$.
- $T$, $c=4$: central pawns files $1..8$ at $n_0=20$, files $1..10$ at $n=22$. Left end $j=1$ ($W2$), window $0..4$; right end $j=8$ ($B4$), window $5..9$ (at $n=22$: $j=10$, window $7..11$). E found 0 T/K moves at both ends in all nodes, every central move P.
- $S$, $c=7$: central pawns files $4..11$ at $n_0=23$, files $4..13$ at $n=25$. Left end $j=4$ ($B4$), window $3..7$; right end $j=11$ ($W2$), window $8..12$ (at $n=25$: $j=13$, window $10..14$). At the right end the pawn has L moves (28219) as well as P moves (52671); Lemma 2(b) allows L, and there are 0 T/K moves. The wall-end files $13,14$ of $S_{23}$ (T and K moves occur there) lie outside the arc and outside both end windows.

**H4 (start).** $\mathrm{start}_n$ has no flag, since no pawn has just double-stepped, and no passed pawn. Every wall pawn is blocked by the opposite-colour pawn on a neighbouring wall file. $T$ core: $B5/W2$, the co-located $W6B7$, then the adjacent pairs $W3/B7$, $B6/W3$, $W2/B6$, and the final $W2$. $S$: the leading $B4$, $B6$, $W3$ are blocked by the seam $W2$ on file $n-1$, the $W3$ on file 2 and the wall $B4$ on file 3; the trailing core after $W6B7$ has the same adjacent-opponent pattern as in $T$. E and R ran the passed-pawn test on all reduced nodes: none has a passer.

**H5 (race rule).** Lemma 2 never uses the race. The insertion shifts files but keeps every pawn's rank and the three-file pattern around the cut, so in Lemma 3 the passed pawns of $c_\mu$ and $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$ and their promotion distances coincide; any rule that depends on the passed pawns and on who moved, "count" included, gives the same class (Note 1 of Section S15, H4). The value is rule-specific, the lemmas are not.

**H6 (invariant).** $I_n$: no node of the reduced game has a flag, and every node agrees with $\mathrm{start}_n$ outside $Z_n$; in particular the arc $A$ is pattern in every node ($T$: the whole wall; $S$: the fixed run $3..n-11$, which contains $A$ for $n\ge23$). $I_{n_0}$ is C1. If $I_n$ holds ($n\ge n_0$): every node is non-terminal with no flag, and $A$ consists of pattern files, so Lemma 3 applies to every node with the chosen $c$; with H4 and induction on the distance from the root, nodes, K-edges and T-flags of $G_{n+2}$ are the $\mathrm{ins}_c$-images of those of $G_n$. An image has no flag; it agrees with $\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ outside $Z_{n+2}$ since the inserted files are copies of pattern files and $\mathrm{ins}_c(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$. So $I_{n+2}$. The computed steps ($20\to22\to24$; $23\to25\to27$) agree with this correspondence.

**H7 (meaning of $\equiv\star3$).** As in Section S13 and in H8 of Note 1 of Section S15, and as the theorem is stated: $G\equiv\star3$ means that for every heap $\star h$, $h<256$ (a passed pawn is worth $\pm256$), $G+\star h$ and $\star3+\star h$ have the same outcome: P for $h=3$ and N otherwise. C1 gives signature NNNPNN for $h=0..5$; for $6\le h<256$, the heap move to the P-position $G+\star3$ gives N. The start has no flag and neither do the reduced nodes, so the e.p. convention across a heap move is immaterial (E and R ran both readings "keep" and "expire": identical results). This relation is weaker than equality of partizan games in standard CGT: the numbers 1 and 2 both have outcome L against every nim heap, yet $1\ne2$. The proof shows neither that the ring games are impartial nor that the nim-heap test determines their standard value, so no standard-value claim is made.

## 4. Finite checks

- **C1T** ($n_0=20$; E, `check_S3T3.py` for $T$, $n=20$, $c=4$): 1305 nodes, 4018 K-, 1212 T-moves, zone $\{10,11,13..18\}$, NNNPNN, files $0..9$ exact pattern in every node; Lemma 2: 10440 q-positions, 15660 moves, 0 (a)/(b) failures; Lemma 3: 1305 nodes onto 1305 at $20\to22$ and $22\to24$, 0 mismatches; control fails first at $c=9$ (1328 of 2610). A pump: 1305 nodes, zone $\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-2\}$, ep=0, NNNPNNNN for $n=12..40$, insertion $20\to22$ at $c=4$. R: the same counts, zones and signature at $T_{20},T_{22},T_{24}$, exact insertion $20\to22$ and $22\to24$.
- **C1S** ($n_0=23$; E, `check_S3T3.py` for $S$, $n=23$, $c=7$): 40445 nodes, 141252 K-, 86822 T-moves, zone $\{0,1,2,13,14,16..22\}$, NNNPNN, files $3..12$ exact pattern; Lemma 2: 323560 q-positions, 485340 moves, 0 failures; Lemma 3: 40445 nodes onto 40445 at $23\to25$ and $25\to27$, 0 mismatches; control fails first at $c=12$. A pump: 40445 nodes for $n\ge19$, zone $\{0,1,2\}\cup\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-1\}$, ep=0, NNNPNNNN for $n=13..41$, insertion $23\to25$ at $c=7$. R: the same counts, zone and signature at $S_{23}$; for $23\to25$ and $25\to27$ R recomputed the K/T children at every mapped node for both sides (80890 node/side pairs per step), exact correspondence and closure.
- **C2** (every size below $n_0$): E (`base_S3T3.py`): $T_{12},T_{14},T_{16}$ NNNPNN under "keep" and "expire"; $S_{13},S_{15}$ NNNPNN under both readings. R: $T_{12},T_{14},T_{16},T_{18}$ and $S_{13},S_{15},S_{17},S_{19},S_{21}$, all NNNPNN under both readings (unreduced whole-board search; 763845 states at $T_{18}$, 15775446 at $S_{21}$). A gives NNNPNN for every one of these $n$ through the reduced game and Lemma 1. So each size below $n_0$ is CHECKED-2 (A and R), and $n\le16$ ($T$), $n\le15$ ($S$) also by E.

## 5. Proof of the Theorem

Let $n\ge n_0$ be of the right parity. $I_{n_0}$ is C1; H6 gives $I_n$ for all $n\ge n_0$ and $G_n\cong G_{n_0}$ (nodes, K-edges, T-flags). By C1 and Lemma 1, $G_n+\star3$ is a P-position and the signature is NNNPNN as in C1; H7 gives all heaps $h<256$: $G_n\equiv\star3$. For the sizes below $n_0$, $T_{12},T_{14},T_{16},T_{18}$ and $S_{13},S_{15},S_{17},S_{19},S_{21}$, use C2 and H7. $\blacksquare$

## 6. Gaps and caveats

1. **No gap found in the hypotheses.** What is new relative to the $M_n/O_n$ proof (Section S14) is the $(n+1)$-pawn tail with the co-located $W6B7$, the leading $B4\,B6\,W3$ of $S$ (in the zone, fixed by $\mathrm{ins}_7$), and the $S$ wall-end files $n-10,n-9$ in the zone, which is why $S$ uses the fixed-arc invariant and $n_0=23$ rather than the arc-in-wall bound $n\ge21$.
2. **Lemmas 1-3 are cited, not re-proved**; their hand proofs are those of Section S13 and 2b, refereed as sound for $P_n$ and $Q_n$ (Notes 1 and 2 of Section S15). The proof depends on 2b, which is not re-proved here.
3. **C1, C2 are computer facts**: the theorem for $n\ge n_0$ is "proved modulo C1"; the sizes below $n_0$ are finite computations. A, E and R agree on every checked position. A, E and R are independently written (C, Python, and Python by another AI model). The `check_S3T3.py` runs are E's independent rebuild of the reduced graph and the Lemma 2/3 hypotheses; the `base_S3T3.py` runs are E's direct search.
4. **The claim is nim-heap outcome equivalence** (H7), not equality to $\star3$ as a standard partizan game.
